Expanded checklist for instruction based on the 1978 Cessna Model 182Q POH (D1114-13), Garmin GFC 500 AFMS 190-02291-06 Rev. 8 (S/N 18266034, N1080M), Garmin GI 275 AFMS 190-02246-12 Rev. 8 (S/N 18266034, N1080M) and the FPI Cessna 182 Checkout Form and N1080M Familiarization Sheet rev. 11/18/2026

items.prompt: # reflects an entry on the C182 checkout form or the N1080M familiarization sheet rev. 11/18/2026.
N1080M: 1978 C182Q, S/N 18266034. O-470-U, 230 HP, max 2400 RPM. Speeds are KIAS.
No vacuum system: the turn coordinator is electric. NAV 2 drives a separate analog CDI.
Electrical system is 28 volt (24 V battery).
The POH is the 1978 Model 182Q (S/N 182-66034), which covers the 28 volt system.
New 2 blade propeller fitted at this annual, expected to match the old one.
TBC: any RPM limits in its paperwork.
Annunciators, volts and amps are on the GI 275 engine monitor (EIS).
The analog altimeter is the primary altimeter: set it with every altimeter setting.
GI 275 steps follow N1080M's GI 275 AFMS 190-02246-12 Rev. 8. Section numbers cited are from Rev. 11: TBC.
Club limits: hottest CHT below 380°F for extended periods, redline 400°F. Refuel after every flight.
N1080M runs hot. Holding CHT below 380°F usually needs cowl flaps open and a mixture richer than best lean.
Stall speeds are KIAS, power off, 2,950 lb (POH Fig. 5-3). The horn sounds 5 to 10 knots above the stall.
The checkout form lists VX 57 at S.L.
The POH gives 54 for best angle; 57 is the short field obstacle speed with flaps 20°.
FLOW: cockpit first, then walk the airplane left wing, tail, right wing, nose, then a final look.
Fuel and oil are checked every flight.
Find the AUTOPILOT circuit breaker before flight. Pulling it is the last step of the trim runaway drill (GFC 500 AFMS).
The alternate static source valve is below the pilot side panel. Pull it ON only if static instruments are suspect (POH).
Tach time: EIS outer knob to the Summary page, Timers, TACH. It should match the last logbook entry.
Do not slam the baggage door.
Look in the tank. N1080M has long range tanks: 75 gal usable (80 total), 37 gal usable per side in level flight.
Club: add 1 qt when the level falls to 9. Keep 2 qt in the baggage area and replace one if you use it.
FLOW BY ZONE: cabin (seat, belts), left panel (avionics, autopilot), floor (brakes, cowl flaps, fuel). Then engine controls (mixture, propeller, carb heat, throttle), then master and start.
Do the flow, then confirm with the checklist.
POH: one or two strokes in warm weather, up to six when cold. A warm engine needs no priming.
Enter the fuel you saw in the tanks at preflight. Outer knob to the Fuel page, then set the estimated fuel.
Fuel Est and Act Used help (GI 275 AFMS 7.16.7).
The fuel computer only subtracts fuel flow from what you enter.
It is never the primary fuel quantity: the tanks gauges are (GI 275 AFMS).
Sky-Tec starter placard: crank 10 seconds max, cool 20 seconds between tries, up to 6 tries, then cool 30 minutes.
If no oil pressure within 30 seconds (about 60 in very cold weather), shut down and investigate.
Avoid carb heat after start unless icing conditions exist; it is unfiltered air (POH).
Overprimed or flooded: see Flooded Engine Clearing.
Weak, intermittent firing with puffs of black smoke means overprimed.
Clear it, then restart without more priming (POH).
Reduce the throttle to idle when the engine fires. Allow the starter to cool between long cranking attempts.
Club practice: lean on the ground to avoid plug fouling. Full rich for the runup.
PFT shows in the autopilot status box on the GI 275 ADI during the preflight test. It must pass before you use the autopilot, flight director or electric trim.
An amber AP with a red X means it failed (GFC 500 AFMS).
For IFR, a yellow or red battery icon must be checked in the battery menu: at least 30 minutes left (GI 275 AFMS 4.1.1).
Placard: DISPLAY BACKUP, POSITION 1: ON, POSITION 2: AUTO. Leave it in AUTO.
ON forces the PFD (attitude) to the backup GI 275. AUTO reverts on a detected fault (GI 275 AFMS 1.2).
The GDL 88 self tests at power up and shows failures as annunciations (Garmin ICA 190-01310-01).
The analog altimeter is the primary altimeter.
Placard: STAY OFF BRAKES. Do not ride the brakes while taxiing.
Run the yoke trim switch both ways and watch the trim wheel follow.
The AFMS does not require this test; it is a recommended check.
Outer knob to the CHT/EGT page, then inner knob to Normalized mode (GI 275 AFMS).This zooms the EGT and CHT bars so small changes show. On one magneto every EGT should rise.
This checks the health of every spark plug and lead.
A column that drops or does not rise points to a fouled plug or a lead problem.
Move the propeller back, watch RPM fall and manifold pressure rise, then return it full in.
For night or instrument flights, load the system with the landing light for 3 to 5 seconds at 1700 RPM. The ammeter should stay within a needle width of the first reading (POH).
Inner knob back to Monitor mode, outer knob to the Main page.
The GI 275 HSI selects its own CDI source. The autopilot follows the source shown on the HSI, not the GTN (GI 275 AFMS 4.2.2).
Above 5,000 ft D.A., lean for maximum power in a full throttle static runup (POH takeoff distance chart).
The POH allows 0° to 20° for a normal takeoff. Club convention is 10°.
Feed power in smoothly over about 3 seconds.
Check full throttle early in the roll; rough running or slow acceleration is a reason to stop (POH).
Club check: with the mixture set correctly, EGT on the takeoff roll should be in the low 1400s °F.
Throttle sets manifold pressure; the propeller sets RPM.
Climb power is 23 in or full throttle, whichever is greater, at 2400 RPM (POH).
Soft field: lift off as soon as practical, tail low, then level off to accelerate.
Flaps above 20° are not approved for takeoff (POH).
Flaps 20° cut the ground run and the distance over a 50 ft obstacle by about 20 percent (POH).
Full rich up to 5,000 ft; above that, lean for smoothness and power (POH).
N1080M runs hot: cowl flaps open, mixture rich. If CHT climbs, lower the nose and enrichen.
Watch CHT in a slow climb and lower the nose to 85 or more if it rises.
Best angle (VX) is 54 KIAS at sea level, 62 at 10,000 ft, flaps up.
No more than 75% power. Normal cruise is 55% to 75% (POH).
Club standard: lean in cruise only below 65% power.
Recommended lean: lean until rough, enrichen to smooth, then the same again. Or 50°F rich of peak EGT.
Peak EGT only at 65% power or less. Lean of peak is not approved (POH).
N1080M runs hot: expect cowl flaps open and a mixture richer than best lean to hold CHT below 380°F.
Choose the lowest smooth RPM in the green arc for the power you want (POH).
Re-lean after any change of altitude, power or carb heat.
The left tank drains faster than the right on BOTH (familiarization sheet).
With the autopilot engaged, the fuel imbalance limit is 10 gallons (GFC 500 AFMS).
Scan manifold pressure for carb ice.
With a constant-speed propeller, ice shows as a manifold pressure drop, not an RPM drop.
Use full heat to clear it, then the least heat that keeps ice away.
FLOW (LBCC GUMPFS): lights, belts, carb heat, cowl flaps, then gas (fuel), mixture, propeller, flaps.
Say it aloud. The propeller forward is the item most often missed, and without it go-around power is not there.
At high elevation airports set best power instead: full rich loses power for a go around.
Disengage the autopilot below 800 ft AGL, or 200 ft AGL on an approach (GFC 500 AFMS).
Pitch forces are heavier than in a C172 or PA-28.
Trim nose-up on final so you can hold the nose off and land on the main wheels.
Hold the nose off and never accept a nose-low touchdown. A bounce means go around.
In a strong crosswind use the least flaps needed for the field length (POH).
With all three wheels down: flaps up, full up elevator, and brake hard without sliding the tires (POH).
At landing trim and full flaps, go-around power pitches the nose up hard and yaws it left.
Unchecked, this is the elevator trim stall. Feed power in smoothly, push, right rudder, trim at once.
The GO button sets go-around command bars and wings level.
With the autopilot engaged it stays engaged and follows them.
Set the CDI and the lateral and vertical modes for the missed approach (GFC 500 AFMS).
Tach time: EIS outer knob to the Summary page, Timers, TACH (GI 275 AFMS 7.16.9).
LEFT or RIGHT stops cross-feeding so the tanks fill fully (POH 2-8). Return it to BOTH at the next preflight.
Suspect airspeed, altimeter or vertical speed readings (POH).
Airspeed may read up to 3 knots fast and the altimeter 45 ft high in cruise. Use normal approach speeds (POH).
Signs: an unexplained drop in manifold pressure, then roughness.
The propeller governor holds RPM, so RPM does not drop (POH).
If you must keep heat on in cruise, use the minimum that prevents ice and lean for smoothness (POH).
An obvious power loss on one magneto points to a plug or magneto. Go back to BOTH unless roughness is extreme.
Low pressure with normal temperature may be a gauge or relief valve problem.
Land at the nearest airport to inspect (POH).
HIGH VOLTAGE light: the alternator is shut down and the battery carries the load (1978 POH Section 7).
The battery can supply the system for a limited time only. At night, keep power for the flaps and landing light.
With the alternator off the battery is the only power.
The GI 275 engine monitor stops working if the instruments go to backup battery power (GI 275 AFMS 3.1.6).
An amber AP with a red X in the autopilot status box after power up (GFC 500 AFMS 3A).
ESP works only with the autopilot off.
It pushes back past +20° or -15° pitch, 45° bank, 176 KIAS, or below 60 KIAS (above 200 ft AGL).
After about 10 seconds it engages the autopilot in LVL mode (GFC 500 AFMS).
Holding AP DISC/TRIM INT stops ESP while held.
For steep turns or stall training, disable ESP through the GI 275 ADI (familiarization sheet).
The autopilot uses the attitude and navigation source on the pilot's GI 275.
Check its modes against the other instruments and consider disconnecting it (GI 275 AFMS 3.1.1).
The GI 275 engine monitor is blank, frozen or unresponsive (GI 275 AFMS 3.1.9).
The AFMS says only to keep the engine within its limits.
Using known power settings and landing are instructor guidance.
Be prepared for high elevator control forces.
Release the button only after the breaker is out. The breaker removes the autopilot, electric trim and ESP.
Do not overpower the autopilot in flight: the trim runs against you (GFC 500 AFMS).
Expect a higher stall speed with 1/4 in or more of ice on the leading edges.
Flap extension can reduce elevator effectiveness with tail ice (POH).
Lower the nose first and hold the glide. Plan straight ahead with small turns only.
There is seldom enough altitude to return to the runway.
While gliding, look for the cause. If the engine does not restart, make a forced landing without power.
Note the preferred touchdown area and any obstructions, then retract the flaps once safe altitude and airspeed are reached.
The goal is to suck the flames and fuel through the carburetor into the engine (POH).
If the fire is out and you need power: master ON, find the faulty breaker (do not reset it).
Then switch equipment on one item at a time, with a pause after each.
Ventilate after using an extinguisher, and open the vents only when the fire is certainly out (POH).
